purpose: Fix, before any candidate earnings date is inspected, which events enter the GST Market Attention Observatory cohort. This document is observational measurement infrastructure. It does not test, optimize, select for, or claim any profitable trading strategy.

locked_universe.authority: The production constant is the sole authority. This list is generated from it at authoring time and is verified against it mechanically by test_market_response_cohort_protocol.py; it is never retyped or edited by hand.

collection_window.boundary_semantics: Inclusive on both ends. The window is applied to the event's MECHANICALLY DERIVED pre-event anchor session, not to the earnings date and not to the registration date.
collection_window.change_rule: The window may not be widened, narrowed, or shifted once any pre-event observation for any cohort event exists. A change before that point is a new protocol version with its own dated entry; it is never an in-place edit.

target.basis: independently registered eligible events across the locked universe
target.note: The target describes intended coverage. Enrollment is exhaustive over eligible events, so reaching 60 neither stops enrollment nor licenses early analysis.

minimum_registration_lead.semantics: The registration must be written at least 5 XNYS trading sessions before the event's derived pre-event anchor session. Session arithmetic is performed by the production calendar; this protocol reimplements none of it.

derived_anchor.authority: The anchor is derived mechanically from the human-verified registry row and the XNYS calendar. This protocol never computes, overrides or rounds an anchor.

requirements: Published by the issuer or filed by the issuer with the SEC.
Directly fetched or directly observed by a named human; a search-engine snippet, aggregator, third-party calendar, broker estimate or historical cadence is never a source of record.
States release timing explicitly enough for the production registry to classify it without inference.
The exact observed text, URL, retrieval timestamp and verifier identity are recorded in the registry row.
permitted_official_source_types.relationship_to_production: Additive and stricter. Production enforces that a non-empty event_time_source exists and that the release session is an explicit member of VALID_RELEASE_SESSIONS; this allowlist further restricts which source types the cohort will accept. It never weakens a production check.

inclusion_rules.rule: The ticker is a member of the locked 24-ticker universe.
The event is a regular quarterly or annual earnings release.
The release date comes from an official company investor-relations source on the permitted list.
That source explicitly establishes a calendar date.
Release timing is explicit enough for the production registry to classify the session without inference.
The mechanically derived pre-event anchor falls inside the collection window.
The event can be registered at least 5 XNYS trading sessions before its pre-event anchor.
No pre-event snapshot has already been collected for the event.
No GST, Wikipedia, price, volume, volatility, options, analyst-reaction, surprise or news-outcome data was inspected in deciding enrollment.
No previously registered event exists for the same ticker and fiscal quarter.

permitted: official source URL, title, type and retrieval time
enrollment_inputs.rule: Enrollment is a function of the permitted inputs alone. Inspecting any prohibited input before an enrollment decision voids that decision: the event is recorded COMPROMISED_ENROLLMENT_BLINDING and excluded from the confirmatory cohort. It is never silently re-enrolled.

dispositions.meaning: Every inclusion rule is satisfied and the registry row is written.
No official source yet establishes a calendar date. Re-screened on the screening cadence defined in v1.1 (Mondays 09:00 America/Chicago) until the lead-time rule can no longer be met.
An official date exists but the timing is not explicit enough for the production registry to classify the session without inference.
A previously observed official source was withdrawn or is contradicted by another official source. Enrollment waits; a registered event is never deleted on this basis.
Fewer than 5 XNYS sessions remain between the earliest possible registration and the derived anchor.
A registered event already exists for this ticker and fiscal quarter.
Cancellation, merger, delisting, or the release is no longer a normal quarterly/annual earnings event.
The event was discovered only after its anchor session began. It can no longer be enrolled blind and is recorded, not quietly dropped.

The issuer changed the official date or time before the anchor. Recorded as an append-only AMENDMENT row; the anchor is re-derived and the lead-time and window rules are re-applied to the corrected event.

The issuer changed the official date or time after the anchor session began. The correction is recorded as an append-only AMENDMENT, the event is marked compromised and excluded from the confirmatory cohort, and every byte already collected is preserved.
A prohibited input was inspected before the enrollment decision.

prohibited_exclusion_reasons: an interesting or uninteresting attention signal
a source failure occurring after valid registration
an expectation that the event will or will not produce an interesting result
any post-hoc judgement informed by collected data

rules: A correction is a new AMENDMENT row referencing the original by row_id.
The original registration's bytes are never overwritten, edited or deleted.
The effective view folds amendments over the base row in order; the base row's own bytes remain as first written.
An amendment may correct a date, time, session label or source. It may never change the ticker, the fiscal quarter, or the fact that the event was enrolled.
No amendment may be motivated by collected attention or market-response data.

blinding_prohibitions.before_enrollment: No GST, Wikipedia, price, volume, volatility, options, analyst-reaction, surprise or news-outcome data may be inspected before the enrollment decision is recorded.
blinding_prohibitions.after_enrollment: Collected data may never retroactively alter enrollment, the cohort window, the target, or an event's inclusion.
blinding_prohibitions.layer_separation: Layer A / Layer B capture-versus-reveal discipline is defined by the Event Dossier Protocol and is not restated or relaxed here.

rules: An absent verified options benchmark may lower an event to 'core_only_no_option_benchmark'. It never removes an otherwise valid event from the core attention-versus-market-response cohort.
A core-only event remains eligible for 'core_attention_vs_equity_response' and ineligible for 'options_implied_move' and 'joint_attention_plus_options'.
This protocol defines no interval formula, threshold, quote-age limit, skew limit or completeness gate. All of those live in the v0.2 documents and in gst_market_response.completeness, unchanged.

stages.may_read: official IR sources, the XNYS calendar, the existing registry
stages.may_not_read: any attention, market, options or outcome data

stages.governed_by: SPEC v0.2 sections 2 and 7; the strict six-field core gate

stages.decides: which families an event may inform

stages.note: No stage of this protocol produces, evaluates or implies a trading rule.

analysis_separation.one_way_rule: Information flows forward only. A later stage never feeds back into an earlier one.

display_gate.rule: No hypothesis result may be displayed, summarised, plotted or informally described before that hypothesis's own registered sample-size threshold is reached.
display_gate.governance_text: No hypothesis gets tested until a pre-set minimum sample size is hit, decided now, not adjusted later; each hypothesis gets its own dated pre-registration file.
display_gate.note: No numeric per-hypothesis sample-size threshold is currently registered for the market-response families. This protocol deliberately does NOT invent one -- setting that number is a separate, dated pre-registration decision. Until such a threshold is registered for a family, the gate denies display for that family. Absence of a registered number is never read as absence of a gate.

existing_provenance.why_eligible: Registered before any pre-event observation existed and satisfies the same rules. It receives no special treatment, no exemption and no priority.

screening_rows_note: Still empty in this version. v1.1 is published BEFORE the first candidate investor-relations page is inspected, so the cadence cannot be shaped by what the first sweep turns out to find.
non_goals: This protocol does not test, optimise, select for, or claim a profitable trading strategy.
It produces no return forecast, no signal ranking and no buy or sell recommendation.
It does not redefine any v0.2 threshold, interval formula, completeness tier or gate.
It does not authorise any collection before an event's own anchor.

supersedes.statement: v1.1 supersedes v1.0 PROSPECTIVELY from the moment this version is pushed. v1.0 is preserved byte-for-byte and is never rewritten; it remains the record of what the rules were before the cadence was defined. Nothing decided under v1.0 is re-decided under v1.1.
everything_else_unchanged: minimum registration lead of 5 XNYS sessions
relationship to the v0.2 completeness tiers

screening_cadence.why_this_exists: v1.0 said pending candidates are 're-screened on a fixed cadence' but never defined it. An undefined cadence is an opening for discretion: a sweep run when it feels useful is a sweep whose timing can be influenced by what one expects to find. The cadence is therefore fixed HERE, before the first candidate lookup.

initial_sweep.when: immediately after the v1.1 commit is pushed

recurring_sweep.scope: every candidate still on the cadence (see who_stays_on_the_cadence)

missed_sweep_rule.statement: If a scheduled sweep cannot run because of a DOCUMENTED technical failure, it runs on the next available calendar day and the delay is recorded with its cause. A sweep is never silently skipped, and a missed sweep is never back-dated.

who_stays_on_the_cadence: every pending candidate, until it is enrolled or receives a terminal disposition
every already-enrolled event, until its pre-event anchor begins, SOLELY to detect official date/time amendments
screening_cadence.enrolled_event_recheck_scope: Official date and time only. An enrolled event's recheck may confirm the source still says what it said, or surface an issuer change to be handled by the v1.0 append-only amendment rules. It may never revisit enrollment itself.
screening_cadence.inputs_and_blinding: Re-screening uses exactly the v1.0 permitted inputs and the v1.0 blinding prohibitions. Nothing about being a re-screen rather than a first screen relaxes either.
screening_cadence.unscheduled_rescreen_rule: No unscheduled re-screen may be triggered by any item above. A re-screen happens because the calendar says so, never because something looked worth another look.
screening_cadence.target_does_not_stop_enrollment: Reaching 60 registered events does NOT stop enrollment. The target is a coverage floor; the cadence continues over the whole collection window.
screening_cadence.cadence_change_rule: Changing the cadence requires a new dated protocol version written before the sweep it would affect. It is never an in-place edit and never a mid-stream adjustment.
